section_summary: This section comprises sheets 15 through 25 of the State Department's "List of Papers" (docket list) cataloguing records in decimal file 894.628 (Fishing Vessels - Japan) from April 1935 to February 1937. The recorded entries document inter-agency and diplomatic communications between the State Department, Navy, Treasury, Commerce, and the Japanese Embassy regarding port visits, courtesies, and itinerary changes for Japanese vessels, notably the training ship Hakuyo Maru and the fur-seal research vessel Hakuho Maru in Alaskan and Aleutian waters. They also reflect American security surveillance of Japanese crab fishing operations in the Bering Sea, concerns over reciprocal visits to closed ports in the Japanese Mandated Islands, and the legal application of the 1911 Fur Seal Convention.

subfiles.summary: This document comprises pages 15 through 25 of the State Department's List of Papers for File 894.628, summarizing documents numbered 114 to 174 concerning Japanese fishing vessels. The entries detail diplomatic exchanges and inter-agency coordination between the State Department, Navy, Treasury, Commerce, and the Japanese Embassy regarding port visits, courtesies, and surveillance of the vessels Hakuyo Maru, Hakuho Maru, and crab fishing fleets in Alaskan and Aleutian waters. They also address security concerns over closed naval areas, potential reciprocal American visits to the Japanese Mandated Islands, and interpretations of the 1911 Fur Seal Convention.
